questions.stem: Taking another person's property without permission and with no intention of returning it is
questions.explanation: Theft (stealing) is taking someone else's property dishonestly without consent.

questions.stem: Telling lies deliberately to deceive others is called
questions.explanation: Falsehood, or deliberate lying, is listed among common wrongs and can be part of crimes such as fraud.

questions.stem: Which of these is a crime?
questions.explanation: Dealing in fake drugs is a crime because it endangers lives and cheats buyers.

questions.stem: The unlawful killing of a human being with intent is called
questions.explanation: Murder is the intentional and unlawful killing of another person, one of the most serious crimes.

questions.stem: Which of the following would BEST reduce crimes committed by idle young people in a town?
options: Providing vocational training and job opportunities
Increasing the number of beer parlours
questions.explanation: Skills and jobs give young people a lawful source of income and keep them busy, which reduces crime.

questions.stem: Peer pressure can lead a young person into crime mainly when
options: he or she joins a debating club
he or she follows bad friends in order to be accepted
questions.explanation: Wanting acceptance by friends who commit crimes can lead a young person to copy their actions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an effect of crime on a community?
questions.explanation: Crime makes people afraid, discourages investment and raises the cost of security.

questions.stem: Internet fraud in which a person pretends online to be someone else in order to collect money from victims is a modern form of
questions.explanation: Advance fee fraud ("419") deceives victims into paying money for promised benefits; it is now often done online.

questions.stem: Why does crime discourage foreign investors from coming into a country?
options: They fear for the safety of their staff and property
Crime reduces the cost of doing business
questions.explanation: Investors avoid places where lives and property are not safe, so crime slows economic growth.

questions.stem: Which of these is a cause of crime?
options: Greed and the desire to get rich quickly
questions.explanation: Greed and the desire for quick wealth drive people to fraud, robbery and other crimes.

questions.stem: Neighbourhood watch groups help to prevent crime by
options: keeping watch over the area and informing the police of suspicious activities
carrying out arrests without the police
questions.explanation: Neighbourhood watch groups support the police by watching and reporting, not by taking the law into their own hands.

questions.stem: Schools can help to prevent crime among students by
options: teaching moral values and counselling students
questions.explanation: Values education, counselling and supervision help students to avoid crime.

questions.stem: A community has many unemployed youths and no lighting on its streets. Which TWO measures would BEST reduce crime there?
options: Skills training for the youths and installing street lights
Closing all schools and banning meetings
Increasing the price of food and closing markets
Removing police posts and stopping patrols
questions.explanation: Skills training tackles a root cause (idleness), while street lighting removes the dark spots criminals use.

questions.stem: Sale of food that has been contaminated is a crime mainly because it
options: endangers the health and lives of consumers
questions.explanation: Contaminated food can cause sickness and death, so selling it knowingly is a crime against consumers.

questions.stem: Forcing a person to have sexual intercourse without consent is the crime of
questions.explanation: Rape is a serious crime of sexual violence punishable by long imprisonment.

questions.stem: Lack of proper parental care can lead children into crime because
options: children become too busy with homework
children spend more time at home
the children may lack guidance and fall into bad company
questions.explanation: Children without guidance and supervision are more easily influenced by criminals and bad friends.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an effect of crime on the victim's family?
options: Emotional trauma and loss of income
questions.explanation: Victims and their families suffer fear, grief, injuries and sometimes loss of income or property.

questions.stem: Making a false copy of a document, such as a certificate, in order to deceive is called
questions.explanation: Forgery is making or altering documents falsely with intent to deceive, and it is a crime.

questions.stem: Drug abuse can lead to crime because
options: users may steal or become violent under the influence or to get money for drugs
questions.explanation: Drugs impair judgement and addiction can drive users to steal or become violent.

questions.stem: Which agency is mainly responsible for preventing crime and arresting offenders in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Nigeria Police Force is the main agency for crime prevention, investigation and arrest of offenders.

questions.stem: If you see a crime taking place, the SAFEST action is to
options: move to a safe place and report to the police or a trusted adult
post the incident online before telling anyone
questions.explanation: Your safety comes first: get away from danger and report quickly to the police or a responsible adult.

questions.stem: The toll-free number to call the Federal Road Safety Corps to report a road crash is
questions.explanation: FRSC's toll-free emergency number is 122; 112 is the general national emergency number.

questions.stem: When describing a suspicious vehicle to the police, the MOST useful detail is the
options: name of the radio station playing in it
plate number, colour and type of the vehicle
questions.explanation: Plate number, colour, make and direction of travel help the police identify and trace a vehicle.

questions.stem: A student who sees a classmate bringing a dangerous weapon to school should
options: take the weapon from him by force
report quietly to the principal or a teacher
tell everyone in the class first
questions.explanation: Reporting quietly to school authorities lets trained adults handle the danger safely.

questions.stem: Why should a witness avoid touching things at the scene of a crime?
options: Because the items will become expensive
To make the scene look neat
To avoid destroying evidence the police need
questions.explanation: Touching or moving things can destroy fingerprints and other evidence.

questions.stem: Observing a crime properly involves noting
options: what happened, where, when and what the people involved looked like
questions.explanation: Good observation records the who, what, where and when, which makes a report useful.

questions.stem: Some people refuse to report crimes they witness. Which of the following is the MOST likely reason?
options: They want the police to succeed
Fear that the criminals may attack them
questions.explanation: Fear of revenge is a common reason; that is why security agencies allow confidential or anonymous reporting.

questions.stem: Why is it important for security agencies to keep the identity of people who report crimes secret?
options: To protect them from attack and encourage others to report
To make the case last longer
To punish the people who report
To stop the police from investigating
questions.explanation: Confidentiality protects informants and gives more people the confidence to report crimes.

questions.stem: Which of these people can a student report a suspected crime to in school?
questions.explanation: Students should report to responsible adults in school such as the principal, teachers or counsellors.

questions.stem: A stranger offers to give you a lift home from school and insists that you enter his car. You should
options: refuse, move away and tell a teacher or parent
follow him to see where he goes
questions.explanation: Never go with strangers; refuse, get away to a safe place and report to a trusted adult.

questions.stem: You receive a text message saying you have won a prize and must pay a "processing fee" to collect it. The best response is to
options: forward it to all your friends
ignore the message, not send money and tell an adult
questions.explanation: Messages asking for fees to collect prizes are common fraud tricks; do not pay or share personal details.

questions.stem: Which agency should be informed if a person is suspected of selling fake or expired drugs?
questions.explanation: NAFDAC regulates food, drugs and related products and acts against fake and expired products.

questions.stem: Which agency should receive a report of a person suspected of trafficking children for forced labour?
questions.explanation: NAPTIP (National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons) handles human trafficking cases.

questions.stem: A witness who reports a crime to the police should give
options: exaggerated stories to make it serious
questions.explanation: False or exaggerated reports can mislead investigations and are themselves an offence.

questions.stem: Which of these is a way of reporting a crime?
questions.explanation: 112 is Nigeria's toll-free national emergency number for reporting crimes and emergencies.

questions.stem: An appropriate response when a fight breaks out among students is to
options: keep away and quickly inform a teacher
questions.explanation: Keeping away avoids injury, and informing a teacher allows the fight to be stopped safely.

questions.stem: Which of these is a sign that a person in your area may be involved in criminal activity and should be reported?
options: He goes to work every morning
He keeps weapons hidden and receives strange visitors at odd hours
questions.explanation: Hidden weapons and secretive movements at odd hours are warning signs that should be reported to the authorities, not confronted.

questions.stem: The motto often used to encourage people to report suspicious activities is
questions.explanation: The slogan encourages citizens to report anything suspicious to security agencies.

questions.stem: Why should a crime be reported as soon as possible?
options: So that the crime will be forgotten
So that the police can act before evidence is lost and suspects escape
So that the report fee is cheaper
So that the victim is blamed
questions.explanation: Quick reporting increases the chance of catching suspects and preserving evidence.

questions.stem: Bayo saw some boys removing a manhole cover on the road at night. Which response is MOST appropriate?
options: Shout at them and chase them alone
Stay at a safe distance, note the details and report to the police or community leaders
questions.explanation: Confronting suspects alone can be dangerous; observing safely and reporting is the right response.

questions.stem: A person convicted of stealing in Nigeria is usually punished with
questions.explanation: Theft is punishable mainly by imprisonment, and the court may also order a fine or restitution.

questions.stem: The most severe punishment that can be given for murder under Nigerian law is
questions.explanation: Murder can attract the death penalty in Nigeria.

questions.stem: The punishment for a person convicted of rape in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: Rape attracts long prison terms, up to life imprisonment, under Nigerian law.

questions.stem: People convicted of human trafficking in Nigeria face
questions.explanation: Trafficking in persons laws provide for imprisonment and fines for offenders.

questions.stem: Drug trafficking in Nigeria is punishable by
options: long-term imprisonment and forfeiture of assets
questions.explanation: Drug trafficking attracts long prison terms, and convicts can lose property bought with drug money.

questions.stem: Food contamination means
options: the presence of harmful substances or germs in food
storing food in a clean place
questions.explanation: Contaminated food contains germs, chemicals or other harmful substances that can cause illness.

questions.stem: Which of these can cause food contamination?
questions.explanation: Dirty hands carry germs that contaminate food.

questions.stem: Drug adulteration is
options: adding inferior or harmful substances to drugs or reducing their active ingredients
storing drugs in a cool place
checking the expiry date of drugs
questions.explanation: Adulterated drugs are mixed with inferior or harmful substances, making them ineffective or dangerous.

questions.stem: Which of these is a danger of using adulterated drugs?
options: The illness may not be cured and the patient may die
The drug becomes cheaper and safer
The drug lasts longer in the body
questions.explanation: Adulterated drugs may not treat the illness and can poison the patient.

questions.stem: Ripening fruits with calcium carbide, a harmful industrial chemical, is dangerous mainly because
options: it makes the fruits taste sweeter
it is approved for all foods
it adds vitamins to the fruits
harmful residues can affect the health of consumers
questions.explanation: Calcium carbide can contain harmful impurities and is not approved for ripening food; it endangers consumers' health.

questions.stem: Why do courts give stiff punishments for crimes such as drug trafficking and human trafficking?
options: To deter others and protect society
questions.explanation: Severe punishments discourage others from committing similar crimes and protect the public.

questions.stem: The place where convicted offenders serve their prison terms in Nigeria is managed by the
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Correctional Service (formerly the Nigerian Prisons Service) keeps and reforms convicted offenders.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a sign that a packaged food may be contaminated or unsafe?
options: An expiry date in the future
questions.explanation: Swollen, rusted or leaking cans may contain dangerous germs, so the food should not be eaten.

questions.stem: A consumer can identify an expired drug by checking the
questions.explanation: Every drug pack should carry an expiry date; drugs past that date should not be used.

questions.stem: The main purpose of punishing offenders besides deterring others is to
options: reform the offender so that he becomes a better citizen
questions.explanation: Modern punishment also aims to reform and rehabilitate offenders so they do not return to crime.

questions.stem: Before a person is punished for a crime in Nigeria, he or she must be
options: tried and found guilty by a court
questions.explanation: Only a court can convict and sentence a person; jungle justice is itself a crime.

questions.stem: Mob action in which a crowd beats or kills a suspect without trial is called
questions.explanation: Jungle justice is illegal; suspects must be handed over to the police and tried by the courts.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason why jungle justice is wrong?
options: It reduces the work of mobs
It is approved by the constitution
An innocent person may be killed without any trial
questions.explanation: Jungle justice denies fair hearing; innocent people have been killed through it, and those who take part commit crimes.

questions.stem: Mixing palm oil with harmful dyes to make it look redder is an example of
questions.explanation: Adding harmful substances to food to improve its appearance or weight is adulteration.

questions.stem: Scratching a panel on a drug pack and sending the code by text message to confirm the drug is genuine helps consumers to detect
options: the name of the shop owner
questions.explanation: Authentication codes on some drug packs allow buyers to check whether the product is genuine or counterfeit.

questions.stem: An unexpected and dangerous situation that needs immediate action is called
questions.explanation: An emergency is a sudden, dangerous situation requiring urgent action to protect life and property.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an emergency?
options: A child drowning in a pond
A road crash with injured people
questions.explanation: An emergency is sudden and dangerous; a planned sports event is a normal, scheduled activity.

questions.stem: The four phases of emergency management are
questions.explanation: Emergency management covers preventing or reducing risks, preparing, responding and recovering.

questions.stem: The type of fire extinguisher commonly seen in homes and offices that can be used on many kinds of fire is the
questions.explanation: Dry powder (ABC) extinguishers can be used on many classes of fire, including electrical fires.

questions.stem: Why should water NOT be used to put out a fire caused by electricity?
options: Water conducts electricity and can cause electric shock
Water causes the fire to stop at once
questions.explanation: Water conducts electricity; the power supply should be switched off and a suitable extinguisher used.

questions.stem: A good fire drill in school teaches students to
options: hide under the desks until the fire stops
leave the building calmly through the nearest exit and gather at the assembly point
run back to collect their bags
questions.explanation: In a fire, leave calmly by the nearest exit without stopping for belongings, and assemble at the agreed point.

questions.stem: When a room is filling with smoke during a fire, a person should
options: stay low and crawl to the exit
questions.explanation: Smoke rises, so the cleaner air is near the floor; crawling low reduces smoke inhalation.

questions.stem: A person who cannot swim sees a friend drowning in a river. The SAFEST way to help is to
options: jump into the river to pull the friend out
shout for help and throw a floating object or rope to the friend
wait for the friend to swim out
questions.explanation: Untrained rescuers can drown too; reaching or throwing something that floats and calling for help is safer.

questions.stem: After a building collapses, onlookers should
options: climb the rubble to take pictures
start removing blocks without any safety plan
keep away from the site and allow rescue workers to do their job
questions.explanation: Crowds hinder rescue and may be injured by further collapse; trained responders should lead rescue.

questions.stem: Which of these is a cause of building collapse in Nigeria?
options: Use of substandard materials and poor supervision
questions.explanation: Substandard materials, poor design and lack of supervision are major causes of building collapse.

questions.stem: Signs of food poisoning include
questions.explanation: Food poisoning usually causes vomiting, stomach pain and diarrhoea, sometimes with fever.

questions.stem: Several pupils became ill after eating at a party. Which action would help health workers MOST?
options: Throwing away all the leftover food at once
Giving the pupils more of the same food
Taking the pupils to hospital and keeping a sample of the food eaten
Keeping the pupils at home without treatment
questions.explanation: Prompt treatment saves lives, and a food sample helps health workers identify the cause.

questions.stem: The federal agency that coordinates responses to disasters in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: NEMA (National Emergency Management Agency) coordinates disaster response nationally.

questions.stem: At state level, emergency management is handled by the
questions.explanation: Each state has a SEMA that works with NEMA in managing emergencies.

questions.stem: When there is a flood warning in your area, the BEST action is to
options: go swimming in the flood water
move to higher ground and follow instructions from the authorities
questions.explanation: Moving to higher ground and following official advice protects lives during floods.

questions.stem: Which of these is part of PREPAREDNESS in emergency management?
options: Keeping a first aid box and knowing emergency numbers
Burying the dead after a disaster
Distributing relief materials after the event
questions.explanation: Preparedness means getting ready before an emergency, e.g. first aid kits, drills and emergency contacts; the others are recovery actions.

questions.stem: If gas is leaking from a cooking gas cylinder, you should
options: light a match to find the leak
turn off the valve, open the windows and avoid lighting any flame or switch
questions.explanation: A spark can ignite leaking gas; turn off the source, ventilate the area and avoid flames or switches.

questions.stem: The main aim of the RECOVERY phase of emergency management is to
options: help affected people and communities return to normal life
train people for future drills only
questions.explanation: Recovery involves rebuilding, rehabilitation and support so that communities return to normal.

questions.stem: Which of the following helps to prevent drowning?
options: Swimming only in safe areas with a lifeguard present
Swimming after a heavy meal in a storm
questions.explanation: Swimming only in supervised, safe places and covering wells reduces the risk of drowning.

questions.stem: Which agency is mainly responsible for putting out fires in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Federal Fire Service and state fire services fight fires and carry out rescue operations.

questions.stem: The protection of a country, its people and resources from internal and external threats is called
questions.explanation: National security means safeguarding a nation's people, territory, institutions and resources from threats.

questions.stem: The use of violence against civilians to create fear for political or ideological aims is called
questions.explanation: Terrorism uses violence and fear against people to achieve political, religious or ideological goals.

questions.stem: Deliberately setting fire to property is the crime of
questions.explanation: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to buildings or property.

questions.stem: Pipeline vandalism affects Nigeria's national security mainly because it
options: reduces government revenue and causes fires and pollution
questions.explanation: Vandalism of pipelines causes loss of revenue, fuel scarcity, explosions and environmental damage.

questions.stem: Illegal bunkering means
options: stealing crude oil or petroleum products and selling them illegally
storing fuel legally in a petrol station
refining oil in a government refinery
questions.explanation: Illegal bunkering is the theft and illegal sale of crude oil or petroleum products.

questions.stem: Importation of expired foods and drugs threatens national security because it
questions.explanation: Expired foods and drugs can cause illness and death, putting citizens at risk.

questions.stem: Which agency is responsible for protecting oil pipelines and other critical national assets against vandalism?
options: Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC)
questions.explanation: NSCDC has the mandate to protect critical national assets and infrastructure such as pipelines.

questions.stem: The agency that investigates financial crimes such as money laundering and advance fee fraud is the
questions.explanation: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) fights financial crimes.

questions.stem: The agency that fights corruption in public offices, including bribery by public officers, is the
questions.explanation: The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) handles corruption in the public sector.

questions.stem: Human trafficking is a threat to national security because it
options: exploits citizens and is linked to organised crime networks
questions.explanation: Trafficking feeds organised crime, abuses citizens and damages the country's image and human resources.

questions.stem: How does drug trafficking threaten national security?
options: It fuels violent crime and can fund criminal and armed groups
questions.explanation: Drug money funds crime and violence, and drug abuse weakens the youth population.

questions.stem: The agency responsible for border control and the movement of people into and out of Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The Nigeria Immigration Service controls entry and exit of people and issues passports.

questions.stem: Which agency fights smuggling of goods across Nigeria's borders?
questions.explanation: The Nigeria Customs Service collects duties and fights smuggling.

questions.stem: Which of these BEST shows how citizens can contribute to national security?
options: Reporting suspicious movements and obeying the law
questions.explanation: Citizens contribute by being alert, reporting suspicious activities and obeying the law.

questions.stem: Kidnapping is
options: taking away a person by force or deceit and holding him or her unlawfully
questions.explanation: Kidnapping is the unlawful seizing and holding of a person, often for ransom.

questions.stem: Spreading false and alarming information that causes panic in the country is dangerous to national security because it
options: can lead to fear, violence and loss of trust
questions.explanation: Fake news can cause panic, conflict and violence, threatening peace and security.

questions.stem: Which of these crimes most directly damages the environment of the Niger Delta?
options: Illegal oil refining and pipeline vandalism
questions.explanation: Illegal refining and vandalism spill oil, pollute land, rivers and air, and destroy farming and fishing.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Armed Forces are made up of the
questions.explanation: The Armed Forces of Nigeria consist of the Army, Navy and Air Force, which defend the country.

questions.stem: Cybercrime threatens national security when criminals
options: attack government and bank computer systems
questions.explanation: Attacks on critical computer systems can disrupt services and steal money or sensitive information.

questions.stem: Demonstrating security awareness means
options: being alert to one's surroundings and reporting suspicious things
questions.explanation: Security awareness involves alertness, caution and prompt reporting of suspicious activities.

questions.stem:
(a) What is crime? [2 marks]
(b) Mention four examples of common crimes in Nigeria. [4 marks]
(c) State four causes of crime. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Crime is an act or omission that breaks the law and is punishable by the state
1 mark: (b) Theft / stealing
1 mark: (b) Advance fee fraud (419)
1 mark: (b) Murder / rape
1 mark: (b) Sale of contaminated food or fake drugs
1 mark: (c) Unemployment and poverty
1 mark: (c) Greed / desire for quick wealth
1 mark: (c) Peer pressure / bad company
1 mark: (c) Drug abuse / poor parental care
questions.explanation: Crime is any act forbidden by law and punishable by the state. Accept any four valid examples and causes.

questions.stem:
(a) State four effects of crime on a society. [4 marks]
(b) Explain three ways members of a community can cooperate with security agents to prevent crime. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Fear and insecurity
1 mark: (a) Loss of lives and property
1 mark: (a) Discourages investment / slows economic development
1 mark: (a) Bad image for the community or country
2 marks: (b) Reporting suspicious persons and activities promptly to the police
2 marks: (b) Forming neighbourhood watch groups that work with the police
2 marks: (b) Giving correct information as witnesses / supporting school and community security programmes
questions.explanation: Crime causes fear, losses and underdevelopment. Communities cooperate with security agents by reporting, organising lawful neighbourhood watches, giving accurate information and supporting security programmes.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe four ways of reporting a crime. [4 marks]
(b) List four pieces of information a person should give when reporting a crime. [4 marks]
(c) Give two reasons why people should report crimes. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Calling the national emergency number 112
1 mark: (a) Going to the nearest police station
1 mark: (a) Telling a teacher, parent or community leader
1 mark: (a) Using official hotlines or apps of security agencies
1 mark: (b) What happened
1 mark: (b) Where it happened
1 mark: (b) When it happened
1 mark: (b) Description of suspects or vehicles involved
1 mark: (c) To help catch offenders and prevent further crime
1 mark: (c) To protect lives and property in the community
questions.explanation: Crimes can be reported in person, by phone or through trusted adults. Useful reports give what, where, when and descriptions.

questions.stem:
(a) Match each crime with its usual punishment in Nigeria: (i) murder (ii) theft (iii) drug trafficking (iv) human trafficking. [4 marks]
(b) Explain the meaning of (i) food contamination (ii) drug adulteration. [4 marks]
(c) State two ways consumers can protect themselves from fake drugs. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a)(i) Murder: death sentence
1 mark: (a)(ii) Theft: imprisonment
1 mark: (a)(iii) Drug trafficking: long-term imprisonment (and forfeiture of assets)
1 mark: (a)(iv) Human trafficking: imprisonment (with fines)
2 marks: (b)(i) Food contamination: presence of harmful germs or substances in food
2 marks: (b)(ii) Drug adulteration: adding inferior or harmful substances to drugs or reducing their active ingredients
1 mark: (c) Buy drugs only from licensed pharmacies
1 mark: (c) Check the NAFDAC number, seal and expiry date
questions.explanation: Award marks for the correct type of punishment; exact prison terms set by law vary. Contamination and adulteration both make food or drugs unsafe.

questions.stem:
(a) What is emergency management? [2 marks]
(b) List four types of emergencies. [4 marks]
(c) Name two agencies involved in emergency management in Nigeria. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The organisation and management of resources and actions to prevent, prepare for, respond to and recover from emergencies
1 mark: (b) Fire outbreak
1 mark: (b) Drowning
1 mark: (b) Building collapse
1 mark: (b) Road accidents / food poisoning / flood
1 mark: (c) National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) / State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA)
1 mark: (c) Federal Fire Service / Federal Road Safety Corps / Nigerian Red Cross Society / NSCDC
questions.explanation: Emergency management covers prevention, preparedness, response and recovery. Accept any relevant emergencies and agencies.

questions.stem: Describe the appropriate response in each of the following emergencies: (a) a fire outbreak in a classroom [4 marks] (b) a person drowning in a stream [3 marks] (c) a classmate showing signs of food poisoning [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Raise the alarm
1 mark: (a) Leave calmly through the nearest exit, staying low under smoke
1 mark: (a) Go to the assembly point and do not go back for belongings
1 mark: (a) Call the fire service / use a suitable extinguisher only if trained and safe
1 mark: (b) Shout for help
1 mark: (b) Throw a floating object or rope; do not jump in if not a trained swimmer
1 mark: (b) Once rescued, get medical help immediately
1 mark: (c) Inform a teacher or adult at once
1 mark: (c) Take the classmate to a clinic or hospital quickly
1 mark: (c) Keep a sample of the food eaten for health workers
questions.explanation: Responses should protect the rescuer's safety first, raise the alarm and get trained help quickly.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of national security. [2 marks]
(b) Mention four crimes that affect national security in Nigeria. [4 marks]
(c) Name four security agencies in Nigeria and state one function of each. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The protection of a nation's people, territory, resources and institutions from internal and external threats
1 mark: (b) Pipeline vandalism / illegal bunkering
1 mark: (b) Terrorism / kidnapping
1 mark: (b) Drug trafficking / human trafficking
1 mark: (b) Arson / importation of expired foods and drugs
1 mark: (c) Nigeria Police Force: maintains law and order and arrests offenders
1 mark: (c) NSCDC: protects critical national assets such as pipelines
1 mark: (c) NDLEA: fights drug trafficking
1 mark: (c) Nigeria Customs Service: fights smuggling / Immigration: controls borders / Armed Forces: defend the nation
questions.explanation: Accept any four security agencies with a correct function (e.g. Police, Army, Navy, Air Force, NSCDC, DSS, NDLEA, Customs, Immigration, EFCC, ICPC).

questions.stem:
(a) Explain three effects of pipeline vandalism and illegal bunkering on Nigeria. [6 marks]
(b) Suggest four ways citizens can show awareness of crimes that affect national security. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Loss of government revenue from oil, slowing development
2 marks: (a) Fires and explosions that kill people and destroy property
2 marks: (a) Pollution of land and water, destroying farming and fishing
1 mark: (b) Being alert and reporting suspicious activities to security agencies
1 mark: (b) Refusing to buy stolen or illegally refined products
1 mark: (b) Avoiding the spread of fake news
1 mark: (b) Cooperating with security agents / joining lawful community security efforts
questions.explanation: Vandalism and bunkering cause revenue loss, disasters and pollution. Citizens show awareness by vigilance, reporting, refusing stolen goods and avoiding fake news.
